newsitem.title: USA: California wildfire burns out of control.
newsitem.headline: California wildfire burns out of control.

text.p: Fire crews from across California, including prison inmates, battled a wildfire on Friday that was raging out of control and threatening an oilfield, officials said.

The blaze, which started on Tuesday, was being fueled by trees and shrubs made tinder-dry by temperatures topping 100 degrees Fahrenheit (37.7 degrees Centigrade) and low humidity. It had consumed nearly 14,000 acres (5,665 hectares) by mid-morning on Friday, having grown by 4,000 acres (1,600 hectares) in 24 hours.
"Right now it's totally out of control. We're throwing everything we can at it but so far we we've been unable to stop it spreading," said Ventura County Fire Department spokesman Joe Luna.
The fire, burning 50 miles (80 km) northwest of Los Angeles, was only 12 percent contained and there was no forecast of when it would be fully under control, Luna said.
Luna said the main concern was an oilfield in the Sespe Wilderness area dotted with hundreds of small wells.

"These things can burn and catch fire. They are covered in oil and they will ignite," Luna said. He said fire engines were standing by to protect the wells, which are owned by a number of small companies. The oilfield was in the path of the flames, although the blaze was still more than a mile (1.6 km) away, Luna added.

A second fire, in central California 150 miles (240 km) northwest of Los Angeles near the city of Santa Maria in Santa Barbara County, had blackened 36,000 acres (1,450 hectares) by Friday morning. It was 45 percent contained, with full containment expected over the weekend.

The area was mostly ranchland and the main concern was for the safey of livestock, officials said. "The animals have pretty much all been rounded up and put near the ranches, which we are protecting," a Santa Barbara County fire spokeswoman said.

Near San Francisco, a fast-moving brush fire destroyed three expensive homes and damaged two others in a hilly area of Los Gatos. Damage was estimated at $2.5 million, Santa Clara County Fire Department spokeswoman Bonnie Terra said. No one was injured.
The fire was under control by Friday morning but Terra said fire crews would remain on the scene throughout the day to make sure there were no hot spots.
At its height, about 200 firefighters battled the blaze, supported by more than 50 fire engines, four helicopters and six air tankers, Terra said.
About 500 residents were evacuated, half of them from two convalescent homes in the area. All had been allowed to return home by Friday.
Luna said the prevailing winds were pushing the Ventura County fire away from the small towns of Piru and Fillmore but firefighters were keeping a wary eye out in case they changed direction.

Luna said fire departments from all over California had sent detatchments to cover the blaze, in addition to the National Forestry Service, the California Bureau of Land Management and the California Department of Corrections.
Jail inmates were deployed in digging firebreaks and clearing brush. "It's back-breaking work," Luna said.
In addition to the manpower, the battle was also being fought from the air with nine helicopters and six fixed-wing air tankers dropping water and flame retardants.

Luna said the cause of the fire was being investigated but had not been determined. So far, he added, there were no injuries to firefighters or residents and no homes or structures had been lost. About 30 people evacuated from the Piru Lake recreation area on Thursday remained out of their homes on Friday.
